can we go thru the current ─────────────────────────────

The scan is the remaining bottleneck — 1538ms of 1550ms.
Snapshot write is only 12ms.

For single-token search (codedb search trigram), the path
is already the skip_outlines=true branch, so it does not
commit outlines or build the word index. It just:

1. Walks the filesystem serially
   (collectInitialScanEntries)
2. Workers read files + build trigram shards
3. Main thread merges shards

So the next meaningful optimizations are either:

• Parallelize filesystem stat collection — collect paths in
  the serial walk, then fan out stat calls to workers. Same
  pattern as loadSnapshotFast freshness scan. Probably
  saves ~100-300ms.
• Defer symbol/deps index — only relevant for
  multi-word/search_skips_outlines=false path, which *does*
  commit outlines. The serial commit loop does
  rebuildDepsFor + rebuildSymbolIndexFor per file.
  Deferring them to a post-scan parallel pass would be
  bigger but touches more code.
• Optimize trigram extraction — the inner loop over every
  byte. Could use SIMD or batched normalize, but complex
  and gains unclear.

Which direction do you want to go? The filesystem stat
parallelization is the cleanest next step — same pattern we
already used elsewhere.
